title: Session 1 — Participant 20 User + Claude Behavior Graphs
goal: Create a complex, multi-layered photo composite by processing a raw event photo, isolating the subject, generating/blending external assets (smoke, symbols), and applying advanced typography and modern Photoshop effects (pixel stretch) using AI guidance.
context: I am a professional photographer with over seven years of experience, primarily accustomed to Lightroom/ACR grading and traditional portrait editing. I am participating in this study to expand my skills into complex creative photo compositing (turning standard event photos into distinct, movie-poster-style art pieces). I will use a raw event photo of a person in a plague doctor costume and transform it into a stylized, dark, and trendy composite. I will use Claude for workflow strategies, Camera Raw parameters, typography selection, and advanced Photoshop techniques (like the pixel stretch). For generating assets (smoke, symbols) that I cannot photograph myself, I will try Claude first, but use Gemini as a fallback if Claude's image generation is unsatisfactory.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude did help with accelerating the workflow

Step 1.step_name: Adobe Camera Raw (ACR) Processing for Base Vibe
Step 1.step_action: Ask Claude for specific parameter settings in Adobe Camera Raw (ACR) to achieve a "clean, minimalistic, a bit cold vibe." I will use these settings as a baseline to process my raw file (DSC06230.ARW) and open it as a Smart Object in Photoshop. I will not upload the image or mention the final composite yet, keeping this strictly about achieving the initial mood.

nodes.label: Prompt Claude for ACR settings
nodes.detail: Opens a fresh Claude desktop chat next to Photoshop (DSC06230.ARW open in the file browser) and asks for Adobe Camera Raw settings to achieve a clean, minimalistic, slightly cold/moody portrait vibe, without uploading the image or mentioning the final composite.

nodes.label: Generate a full ACR parameter guide
nodes.detail: Responds (chat auto-titled 'Plague doctor cosplay moody color grading') with a detailed parameter guide covering White Balance 4200-4500k,tint +5-+8, Exposure 0--0.25,Contrast +15, Highlights-40, shadows-20, whites-10, blacks -15,  Texture+10, Clarity+12-+15, dehaze +8, Vibrance-25/Saturation-15, Tone Curve, HSL/Color Mixer, Color Grading, Sharpening, Noise Reduction, Vignette, and Grain.

nodes.label: Apply base tonal adjustments in Camera Raw
nodes.detail: Applies the recommended settings one by one on the plague-doctor cosplay portrait, but changes the parameters for exposure, shadows, color grading.

nodes.label: Finish acr processing and open file in Photoshop
nodes.detail: Opens the processed raw file in Photoshop as a Smart Object, creating a 'Background copy' layer alongside 'Background' for non-destructive editing.

Step 2.step_action: Ask Claude for the best modern Photoshop techniques (v25+) to cleanly remove background distractions (such as the people, tent structures, or poles in the background) while preserving the natural environment. I will then execute the distraction removal in Photoshop based on its advice, ensuring it is done non-destructively.

nodes.label: Prompt Claude for the easiest distraction-removal workflow
nodes.detail: In the same chat, asks Claude for the best/easiest modern Photoshop workflow to remove background distractions (people, tent poles) while preserving the environment.

nodes.label: Recommend Quick Selection plus Content-Aware Fill, Spot healing brush, Clone stamp, and Field/Lens Blur, or simply using generative fill
nodes.detail: Responds with the standard technique -- duplicate the layer, Quick Selection/Lasso the distraction, then Content-Aware Fill -- as the fastest, most reliable approach for typical background clutter.

nodes.label: Ask specifically for the Generative Fill workflow
nodes.detail: Follows up asking Claude to give the Generative Fill workflow specifically, rather than the Content-Aware Fill approach just described.

nodes.label: Detail the Generative Fill workflow with cosplay-shot tips: Duplicate layer first, make a loose selection around the distraction, open generative fill, leave the prompt blank, review the generated variations, fine-tune with a layer mask, repeat for other distractions.
nodes.detail: Lays out Photoshop's newer AI-based Generative Fill workflow, noting it usually outperforms Content-Aware Fill on repeating tent fabric/paneling, suggesting prompts like 'dark atmospheric fog', and advising tight selections to avoid AI warping.

nodes.label: Use find distractions in Photoshop for general distractions, people, select remove area with auto mode, and manually touch up remove areas.
nodes.detail: Narrates that Claude's suggestions are correct but somewhat traditional, and decides to use Photoshop's newer one-click Remove tool / 'Find distractions' feature instead since it is faster.

Step 3.step_name: Asset Generation - Environmental Smoke and Fog
Step 3.step_action: Prompt Claude to generate multiple high-resolution image assets of ominous, dense, dark grey/black smoke. If Claude's generation capabilities are unsatisfactory or lack transparency, I will pivot and use Gemini to generate these assets. I will then import these assets into my PSD to create an atmosphere behind the subject.

nodes.label: Prompt Claude for a transparent smoke overlay
nodes.detail: Decides to add dark smoke behind the subject and asks Claude for a transparent PNG of dark smoke that swirls around the subject slightly from right to left, assuming the subject is centered.

nodes.label: Generate dark_smoke_overlay.png
nodes.detail: Produces a usable transparent smoke asset, visible in the file browser as dark_smoke_overlay.png.

nodes.label: Create a new layer
Download and import dark_smoke_overlay.pngr to the new layer
nodes.detail: Judges that this effect looks cool but is not what they want

nodes.label: Open Gemini and submit the same dark-smoke-overlay prompt
nodes.detail: Opens Gemini in a browser tab and submits the same dark-smoke-overlay prompt purely for a side-by-side quality comparison against Claude's asset.

nodes.label: Generate two smoke comparison options
nodes.detail: Gemini returns two swirling black-smoke ring options on a transparent/white background under an A/B 'Which response is more helpful?' comparison UI.

nodes.label: Compare and select Claude's smoke asset
nodes.detail: Reviews both generations and concludes Claude's smoke looked better than Gemini's, choosing Claude's dark_smoke_overlay.png for the composite.

nodes.label: Blend the smoke layer and darken the layer
nodes.detail: Tries Darken blend mode first, then switches to Multiply for a stronger atmospheric effect. Duplicate the layer and adjust the curve to darken.

Step 4.step_name: Asset Generation - Iconography and Central Symbol
Step 4.step_action: Ask Claude (and Gemini, if Claude fails to produce a high-quality result) to generate a metallic, stylized Caduceus (Rod of Hermes - staff with two snakes and wings). Once generated, I will extract it and place it at the top center of my composition.

nodes.label: Prompt Claude for a metallic Caduceus symbol
nodes.detail: Decides to add a medical-staff/Caduceus (Rod of Hermes) symbol above the subject and asks Claude to generate a metallic, stylized version with a staff, two snakes, and wings.

nodes.label: Generate caduceus_rod_of_hermes.png via SVG code
nodes.detail: Writes and iterates a Python/SVG generation script (gen_caduceus.py, rendered to PNG via cairosvg), installing dependencies, drawing snake/wing/orb geometry with metallic gradients, catching and fixing a layering bug (reordering the wing-drawing block before the head-drawing block so wings render behind the heads), then rendering a final high-resolution transparent PNG. Despite judging its own result as reading 'clearly as a metallic gold caduceus,' Claude's closing note admits it is 'a procedurally constructed vector illustration ... it won't have photographic texture detail' since no photorealistic image-generation tool was available in this environment.

nodes.label: Make a background layer and set its brightness and contrast
Prompt Gemini for a metallic Caduceus symbol
nodes.detail: Submits the same prompt to Gemini as was used for Claude

nodes.label: Generate a metallic Caduceus symbol
nodes.detail: Gemini returns a convincing metallic silver Caduceus with wings and two snakes on a transparent background, judged more photorealistic than Claude's procedural vector result.

nodes.label: Chooses Gemini's Caduceus over Claude's
Ask Gemini to change the rod color to silver and creat a png with transparent background
Ask Gemini to generate again without any crops
Download and import the Gemini Caduceus and position it
nodes.detail: Cuts out the approved Gemini Caduceus using Photoshop's Remove/Generative Fill/Deselect quick-action bar, moves it onto its own layer, and positions it at the top of the composition above the subject's head.

nodes.label: Ask Claude for a Caduceus blending workflow
nodes.detail: Asks Claude how to make the newly placed Rod of Hermes blend naturally with the background image, requesting a very convenient workflow.

nodes.label: Provide an 8-step compositing workflow
nodes.detail: Responds with a traditional 8-step compositing workflow: scale/perspective matching, light-direction matching, environment reflections, and edge refinement/softening with a feathered eraser or mask.

nodes.label: Apply Photoshop's Harmonize feature instead
nodes.detail: Judges Claude's steps as correct but notes modern Photoshop has an easier way; selects the Caduceus layer and applies the built-in Harmonize feature, comparing before/after and confirming it blends more seamlessly.

nodes.label: Add curves layers and adjust the opacity for further blending
nodes.detail: Adds additional curves adjustment layers on top of the Harmonized Caduceus layer, and fine-tunes the Caduceus layer's opacity downward slightly.

Step 5.step_action: Consult Claude to identify suitable, free (or Adobe Fonts) typefaces that evoke a "gritty, historical, distressed" feel. I will use the recommended font to spell out a title (e.g., "DOCTOR") with wide tracking, placing it strategically in the composition.

nodes.label: Ask Claude for gritty, historical font recommendations
nodes.detail: Asks Claude for font suggestions matching a gritty/historical/distressed vibe appropriate for the plague-doctor poster title.

nodes.label: Recommend blackletter fonts
nodes.detail: Recommend Blackletter/Gothic fonts for title/hero text (UnifrakturMagnuntia, Pirata One, IM Fell English), and worn serif for caption text (Cormorant, Playfair Display), Vintage typewriter for label (Special Elite, Courier Prime)

nodes.detail: Tests Blackoak Std and a couple of other available substitute fonts in Photoshop
